A4_torusgap1_expanded.task: systematic re-search for a SECOND 'integral' free-group family (type (i)) beyond the known torus family T, with EXPANDED search radius vs. the prior bounded search (m in [-8,8], syllable<=3, exponent<=2).
A4_torusgap1_expanded.enumeration_method: systematic (NOT random): all alternating x/y-syllable xy-words with 1 to 4 syllables, each exponent in {-3,-2,-1,1,2,3}, tested as g'=y^m*g for every m in the range, against the free-group identities g'*theta(g')=1 and tau^2(g')*tau(g')*g'=1 (theta:x<->y, tau:x->y,y->y^-1x^-1).
A4_torusgap1_expanded.result: 42 (m,g) input combinations tested TRUE (excluding the trivial g'=[] case), but these collapse to only 6 DISTINCT reduced values: y^-k x^k and y^k x^-k for k=1,2,3 -- i.e. EXACTLY the already-known torus family T (both orientations), not a new family.
A4_torusgap1_expanded.conclusion: NO second integral family found, absent up to this radius (m in [-12,12], syllable<=4, exponent<=3). This is a negative-up-to-radius-R result, NOT a general non-existence proof; type (i) = T only, as far as this expanded search can tell.

COMP1_composition_law.task: pin down the (3.53) composition law on the 48-shadow set via a canary-arbitrated discriminating experiment (per instruction: canaries decide, not guesswork).
COMP1_composition_law.formula: psi1(x):=x^u1, psi1(y):=f1^-1*y^u1*f1 (u1=2*m1+1); m_new := (2*m1*m2+m1+m2) mod Nord (m tracked as genuine state, NEVER reconstructed from u alone, since Nord can make m and m+Nord/2 share the same u).

end_ring_dims.task: final closure measurement (mathematician instruction 2026-08-22, lemma KER-pi quantitative key): dim End_{F_p[Q]}(V_p), both windows, p in {2,3}. Q-action := conjugation by sigma1,sigma2 on V_p, built via direct per-basis-word conjugation (same canary-validated construction as the H2-obstruction script). End = {M : M*rho(sigma_i)=rho(sigma_i)*M, i=1,2}, solved as a linear system in the dBasis_p^2 entries of M via Kronecker product.
end_ring_dims.bug_found_and_fixed: the FIRST attempt computed NullspaceMat(FullSys) directly, which gives the LEFT nullspace {v : v*FullSys=0} -- the SAME row/column convention bug this campaign has hit and fixed multiple times before -- yielding an impossible result (dim End = 9628 > 9604 = dBasis^2 for window154161, and 2512 > 2500 for window154163, both exceeding the ambient matrix-space dimension, which is mathematically impossible since End is a SUBSPACE of the full matrix space). Fixed via NullspaceMat(TransposedMat(FullSys)) to get the correct RIGHT nullspace {vec(M) : FullSys*vec(M)=0}.
end_ring_dims.canaries: Identity matrix and rho(c) (c=(sigma1 sigma2 sigma1)^2, the central element) both confirmed to lie in End for every (window,p) combination -- PASS. dim End >= 1 confirmed for all four measurements.
end_ring_dims.conclusion: dim End is IDENTICAL at p=2 and p=3 within each window (24 for 154161, 12 for 154163), and notably EQUALS K_ord for that window (K_ord=24 for 154161, K_ord=12 for 154163, as measured much earlier in this campaign via direct x^n membership probes) -- both well within the ambient dBasis^2 bound. Per the mathematician's lemma KER-pi (ker pi* = End_Q(V).e), a LARGER End dimension gives a quantitative explanation for why the obstruction vanishes 'cheaply' -- i.e. why H^2 obstruction classes were found to be zero for every candidate tested (koubou83_h2_obstruction_v1): there is a large-dimensional space of Q-equivariant endomorphisms available to absorb any would-be obstruction into the kernel of pi*.
